sheets.prompt:
Four-panel character reference sheet following the reference layout: three full-body views (front / side / back) left to right, and one large head-and-shoulders close-up filling the right column; the exact same character, outfit and proportions in every panel; plain background. The first reference image is only the panel layout guide: copy its four-panel arrangement, not its grey mannequin shapes. Panel 1 (left): full-body front view, standing in a neutral pose, arms relaxed at the sides, hands open and empty. Panel 2: full-body true side profile. Panel 3: full-body back view showing the black cloth hood lying folded on his shoulders like a cowl. Panel 4 (tall right column): head-and-shoulders close-up, facing the camera, neutral expression, whole face clearly lit and uncovered. Each full-body figure is drawn a little small inside its panel, complete from the top of the head to the soles of the shoes with clear space above and below, standing on a small patch of plain floor with a soft contact shadow; if any part is cut off by the panel edge the sheet is wrong. Plain soft grey-green studio backdrop in every panel, even soft daylight, no scenery, no captions or labels.

Subject: an elderly household officer of the Queen of Hearts, a man about 60 years old, a real human actor in a comic period role. Big-framed and heavy-shouldered, gone soft and paunchy with age, about 186 cm tall. Heavy jowls, deep nasolabial lines, bulbous nose, long upper lip; pale watery blue eyes; thinning iron-grey hair, receding, cropped close at the sides with a bald crown, and grey mutton-chop whiskers. Stubborn, aggrieved, pedantic look of an old craftsman refusing an impossible job. No scars. Wearing: an old-fashioned 1862 senior household servant's livery in dark crimson and black: a long, slightly too-tight dark crimson wool coat with black facings, a black-edged red heart badge and a plain black rank bar at the breast, a black waistcoat straining over a paunch, black knee breeches, black stockings and heavy buckled black shoes, and a black cloth hood worn pushed right back off the head so it lies on his shoulders like a cowl; empty-handed; well-worn and a little shiny at the seams. His whole face and bald crown are uncovered in every panel; he carries nothing.

Style: Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
